canonical_title: US federal judge blocks Pentagon blacklisting of Anthropic
treatment: Treat the California federal-court ruling blocking the Pentagon supply-chain-risk designation as covered. Reinclude for appeal, stay, reinstatement, settlement, contract-policy changes, or a material ruling in the separate Washington D.C. case.
known_facts: U.S. District Judge Rita F. Lin ruled that the Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic was unlawful and blocked the supply-chain-risk designation.
The court found unlawful retaliation under the First Amendment, insufficient pre-deprivation process under the Fifth Amendment, and violations of the governing statutory scheme.
The designation followed Anthropic's refusal to permit Claude to be used for U.S. surveillance or autonomous weapons and had excluded Anthropic from certain military contracts.
Anthropic has a separate lawsuit pending in Washington, D.C. concerning another Pentagon supply-chain-risk designation that could affect civilian government contracts.
reinclude_only_if: The U.S. government appeals, obtains a stay, reinstates or materially changes the designation.
Anthropic and the Pentagon settle or revise Claude military-use contract terms.
The separate Washington D.C. case reaches a material ruling.
notes: NEW in the 2026-08-28 Midday window; court ruling materially changes Anthropic's government-contract position.
